hypotheses.reasoning: The /v1/notify 503s originate in template-svc's calls to the third-party email provider api.mailer.example. Starting at 18:49:12Z, template-svc gets 503 Bad Gateway from POST https://api.mailer.example/v3/send (#1623), repeated at #1630 and #1665, then 502 at #1693. Template-svc is otherwise healthy before and during this: /render calls succeed in ~20-80ms right up to 18:49, GC is normal, and the config reload at 18:38 changed 0 keys. The provider fails fast with HTTP 5xx rather than hanging, which points to the provider being down rather than to template-svc. Template-svc's breaker then opened at 18:50:29 (#1721) at an 85% failure rate. Notification-svc's TemplateClient.render then fails with 'circuit open' (#1760, #1941, #2032, #2259), and api-gateway returns 503 on /v1/notify (#1678, #2267). The breaker's half-open probes keep failing with 502 (#1981, #2244), so the outage is ongoing at the end of the window. The notification-svc and gateway failures are downstream of this. Analytics-forwarder 429s are a separate downstream effect and are not the cause.

A separate, concurrent fault is the identity provider (idp.example) slowing down. It starts earlier, at 18:46:54Z, when auth-svc logs slow calls (3.9s, then 11.9s; #1398, #1441). Calls then time out after 30s (#1512, #1578). This backs up account-svc's connection pool to auth-svc (pool at capacity and checkout timeouts; these are symptoms and not cited). That causes edge-proxy POST /login 503s (for example #1731, #2045). This explains the login outage but not the /v1/notify alert directly. It is ranked lower because the alert is on /v1/notify, and its timing does not explain the notify failure. Two independent issues are likely overlapping in this window.

Analytics-forwarder retries against analytics-ingest (429s, with batches dropped after 5 attempts) amplify load. However, this is a minor, non-user-facing effect and is not the cause of the /v1/notify failures. Listed only for completeness.

verdict.recommendedAction: Escalate to the email provider (api.mailer.example) and confirm its status. Consider failing over to a secondary mail provider, or queueing notifications for later sending. Keep the template-svc circuit breaker in place so the provider is not hammered. Once the provider recovers, replay queued notifications. Separately, investigate the identity-provider slowdown, which is causing a /login outage (auth-svc to idp.example timeouts), and tune its timeouts and circuit breaking.
